label: Pericarditis vs Early Repolarization vs Infarction
rows: LOCALIZED to contiguous leads, convex, reciprocal depression, Q waves.
Inflamed space between visceral and parietal pericardium. PR DEPRESSION, PR ELEVATION in aVR, GLOBAL CONCAVE ST elevation, NO reciprocal depression except aVR and V1.
ST depression in ANY lead other than aVR and V1, or ANY Q wave → consider an acute infarction.
Normal variant ST elevation. Mostly YOUNG MEN. NO clinical significance. Global concave elevation, J-point notch (J wave, fishhook), large T waves, no reciprocal depression, no PR depression.
ST height ÷ T amplitude in V6: OVER 25% = pericarditis; UNDER 25% = early repolarization (more T wave than ST).

label: Brugada Syndrome
rows: Inherited arrhythmogenic disease of the SODIUM channels of the RIGHT VENTRICULAR OUTFLOW TRACT. Young men of SOUTHEAST ASIAN descent.
Both types isolated to V1-V3 ("for a test question").

label: Bundle Branch Block, Pacing & Sgarbossa
rows: Left bundle branch block and ventricular pacing: WIDE QRS, GLOBAL ST elevation and T-wave changes → an infarction is hard to locate.
CONCORDANT elevation 1 mm or more (positive QRS) · CONCORDANT depression 1 mm or more in V1-V3 · DISCORDANT elevation 5 mm or more (negative QRS).
Pacing SPIKE (artifact) before each WIDE QRS, contralateral (discordant) T waves, global ST elevation.

label: Preexcitation & Reentry
rows: Ventricles activated EARLY through an accessory pathway that BYPASSES the atrioventricular node. Short PR + delta wave. Most common: WOLFF-PARKINSON-WHITE.
Pathway = bundle of KENT. Triad: SHORT PR, WIDE QRS, DELTA WAVE (slurred QRS upstroke).
A = LEFT-sided Kent, QRS mostly POSITIVE in V1. B = RIGHT-sided, mostly NEGATIVE in V1.
Down the NORMAL pathway, up the accessory → regular NARROW tachycardia.
Down the ACCESSORY pathway, up the normal → regular, monomorphic, WIDE tachycardia.

May be impossible to tell from supraventricular or ventricular tachycardia (treat a wide one as ventricular tachycardia). Unknown pathway: once cardioversion restores sinus rhythm, look for delta waves.

label: Potassium & Calcium
rows: PEAKED symmetric T (early) → FLAT P → WIDE QRS → SINE WAVE. Can also cause bradycardias, tachycardias, ST elevation, blocks.
Below 3.5 mEq/L. Prolongs repolarization: T FLATTENING, PROMINENT U WAVES, T-U fusion, prominent P, ST depression (ST elevation in aVR).
Phase 2 PROLONGED: LONG ST, NORMAL T, prolonged QTc.
Phase 2 SHORTENED: SHORT ST, shortened QTc, T wave against the QRS.

label: Hypothermia, Pulmonary Embolism, Thyroid
rows: Near 35°C (95°F): SINUS BRADYCARDIA, then long intervals. Below 32°C (90°F): OSBORN waves (terminal QRS notch), often mistaken for an infarction.
TACHYCARDIA (hypoxia → sympathetic), RIGHTWARD axis (right ventricular dilation), ST-T changes (localized ischemia), S1Q3T3 (deep S in I, Q in III, inverted T in III).
SINUS TACHYCARDIA most common; atrial fibrillation second.
Sinus BRADYCARDIA, global LOW VOLTAGE, flat or inverted T, prolonged QTc, low P waves.
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and long QT syndrome
Syllabus objectives with no slide; QT prolongation is listed under calcium, thyroid and drugs.

label: Drug Toxicities
rows: Buildup OR an overly sensitive heart. Inhibits the SODIUM-POTASSIUM PUMP. FREQUENT PREMATURE VENTRICULAR COMPLEXES most common (bigeminy). (Slide says intracellular potassium rises; truth: sodium and calcium rise inside, potassium stays outside.)
Blocks sodium, potassium and calcium channels + BETA BLOCKER. Slows conduction, SLOWS PHASE 3 → QT PROLONGATION, suppresses the sinoatrial node, slows the atrioventricular node.
Fast SODIUM-channel blockade (widens the QRS, as on the slide's tracing) with delayed potassium outflow → QT PROLONGATION; ANTICHOLINERGIC → tachycardia.
